exposure: antenatal care model (general antenatal clinic, private obstetrician, twins clinic)
cohort: 513 women with twin pregnancies delivered at or after 20 weeks' gestation in Sydney, Australia between January 2007 and November 2011
finding: Compared to general antenatal care, attending a specialized twins clinic was associated with decreased Caesarean section rates, late preterm birth, and maternal inpatient stay.
mod_finding: Caesarean section rates were lower in women who attended the twins clinic (55%) compared to those who attended the general antenatal clinic (70%).
birth_weight: Average birthweight was lower in infants of mothers who saw private obstetricians (2283 g) compared to those who attended the twins clinic (2496 g) or general antenatal clinic (2501 g).
